clue.text: Decrease salary, with cut for a division of Human Resources

parts.note: read as de-crease: to iron cloth is to take the creases out

indicators.note: cut says the W standing for with is taken away from the word for pay

parts.note: a wage is pay, a salary

explanation.surface: A manager in a company's personnel department is told to trim staff pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Human Resources' looks like a company department, but here it is human history divided by the materials people used: stone, bronze, then iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistory is split into periods named after the main material used for tools, and this era followed the Bronze Age.

clue.text: My bad review of successful chiropractic treatment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an admission of having been wrong
second meaning, read literally: after good back treatment I stand upright and properly aligned

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a patient whose posture has been fixed would say this; idiomatically it concedes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a formal way of conceding an error, the same as the slang apology.

clue.text: 'Under Control' playing (a bit of a racket)

parts.note: a film or show that is playing is on
a tennis racket is strung with strings, so one string is a bit of it

explanation.surface: A band playing a song called 'Under Control' while making quite a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests noise, but it is the tennis racket with its strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held this way is controlled like a puppet, manipulated at will by another.

clue.text: Harry Kane describing length: 'It's just over a foot'

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing around: the rearranged name surrounds the length letter
to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters of Kane are disturbed

explanation.surface: The footballer Harry Kane describes a shot that just cleared his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Kane is England's football captain, so 'Harry' reads as his first name before it is seen to be an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This joint sits directly above the foot, linking it to the leg.

clue.text: More than one batted, opening with 50, leading test series

indicators.note: leading puts the opening and the fifty in front of the series

parts.note: an eye is an opening, as in the eye of a needle
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the Ashes is the cricket Test series between England and Australia

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman opened, made fifty and led in the Test series.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words make 'batted' mean hit with a bat; here it means fluttered, as one bats an eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: People flutter these hairs on the eyelid flirtatiously, which is called batting them.

clue.text: Lover of Cleopatra many, at first, love to hate?

parts.note: Mark Antony was the lover of Cleopatra, queen of Egypt

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word many

parts.note: first letter of many

explanation.surface: A question about whether Cleopatra's many admirers went from loving her to hating her.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: 'hate' is the opposite word for 'love', so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning is what hate is in relation to love, so the pair illustrates the term.

clue.text: United take a penalty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as two words, in agreement or harmony
second meaning: to make amends by accepting punishment

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a football team taking a spot kick; the two-word phrase means united, the one-word verb means make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong by suffering for it is to expiate, and being in harmony is the split sense.

clue.text: Washing lines reportedly fastened with tags

indicators.note: reportedly means the answer is what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: tied means fastened and marks are tags, so the spoken phrase is tied marks

explanation.surface: Laundry on clotheslines is said to be held on with labels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washing lines' suggests clotheslines; it means grubby lines left after washing, such as the ring round a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimy ring left on a bath or on skin after washing is a line of dirt at the water level.

clue.text: Time Out is almost close to debt

parts.note: nigh means almost, as in nigh on

indicators.note: close to asks for the final letter of debt

parts.note: last letter of debt

explanation.surface: The listings magazine Time Out is said to be nearly broke.
explanation.walkthrough: Time Out is a London listings magazine; here the phrase is read as the period when one is out for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours are the time for an evening out, as in a night out on the town.

clue.text: 'R' for 'run-of-the-mill'

parts.note: the letter R sits at the centre of the seven letters of THE ROAD

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry glossing the letter R as ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the result, R, and the answer describes how to get it: take the centre of THE ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unadventurous, avoiding extremes, is ordinary and commonplace.

clue.text: Historic performance includes a couple of songs

parts.note: a couple of songs asks for two words meaning song; the first is a track on an album
the second song word: a record is a recorded song

explanation.surface: A famous concert is said to have included a pair of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of songs' is read literally: two different words for a song, placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's past achievements, the results they have shown over time, form the history by which they are judged.

clue.text: Move the heart of Freddie Mercury, for one

parts.note: to go is to move

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of the seven-letter Freddie

parts.note: middle letter of Freddie

explanation.surface: A tribute about stirring the emotions of Queen's singer Freddie Mercury.
explanation.walkthrough: Freddie Mercury the singer is the misdirection; the definition is Mercury alone, the Roman messenger deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury was a Roman deity, the winged messenger, so he is one example of a divine being.

clue.text: Briefly, a Parisian hotspot cooked no red meat

definitions.note: the short name of the cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris, a big tourist site

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of the three words are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A note that a fashionable Paris restaurant serves a vegetarian-sounding menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' belongs to the definition: the full name is Notre-Dame de Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité is one of the most visited sights in the French capital.

clue.text: Driving test starts to exhaust learner, making stop along the way

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK cars, named after the Ministry of Transport

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each following word, exhaust and learner

parts.note: first letter of exhaust
first letter of learner

explanation.surface: A learner driver's test is so tiring it leaves them drained.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT tests the car, not the driver, so 'Driving test' is a fair but sly description.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside hotel for motorists is a place to break a journey for the night.

clue.text: Mobile homes where one may retire young

definitions.text: Mobile homes where one may retire young

parts.words: Mobile homes where one may retire young
parts.note: babies' beds often have a mobile hung over them, and to retire is to go to bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile homes' and 'retire young' suggest caravans and early pensions; the mobile is the toy over a baby's bed, and retiring is going to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small barred beds for infants, so they are where a baby is put down at night.

clue.text: Asked out on dates, the French flee

indicators.note: out means the letters of asked are put out of order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for date, doubled for the plural
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone asked out on dates by a French person runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stays in the answer as it is; 'Asked out' looks like an invitation, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper or run off in a hurry is a jokey way of saying to bolt.

clue.text: Spell words wrong here, with typos

definitions.note: words said when a magic spell is worked; the definition is a phrase used as a noun

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of here and typos are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a document is full of misspellings from careless typing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like spelling, matching the typos, but it is a magician's spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror says this phrase at the moment a trick is revealed, as if casting magic.

clue.text: I'm in Journey's End, The Sixth Sense and Rent

indicators.note: End asks for the final letter of the travel word before it

parts.note: journey taken as written; its final letter is used
ESP, extrasensory perception, is called the sixth sense
to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly agreeing to appear in a run of famous plays and films.
explanation.walkthrough: Journey's End is a play, The Sixth Sense a film and Rent a musical, so the clue reads as a cast list.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are eager ways of accepting an offer, saying you want to take part.

clue.text: Single men barred from orgy, catching flogger's interest in passing

indicators.note: catching means the outer letters hold the whip inside them

parts.note: solo means single, alone
the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip used for flogging

indicators.note: barred from means the soldiers are taken out of the orgy word

parts.note: taken as written
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: Single men are refused entry to an orgy that has caught a whip-lover's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred from' takes OR out of ORGY, leaving GY; SOLO plus GY then holds CAT. 'interest in passing' looks like casual interest; the passing is of faeces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the study of, or obsession with, excrement, which is what one passes from the bowel.

clue.text: Drunk trades hands, having drained eggnogs, and slumps

indicators.note: the hands are left and right, so each L for left is traded for an R for right

parts.note: legless is British slang for very drunk

indicators.note: drained means the contents are emptied, keeping only the outside letters of eggnogs

parts.note: first and last letters of eggnogs

explanation.surface: A drunk at a bar swaps hands, finishes the eggnogs and slumps over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trades hands' turns each L (left) of LEGLESS into R (right), giving REGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To go backwards or decline to a worse state is to fall away, as an economy does.

clue.text: Sting's opening for Simon & Garfunkel, maybe after millions

indicators.note: after puts the Garfunkel piece behind the millions piece
opening for asks for the first letter of the name Simon

parts.note: first letter of Simon
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
Art Garfunkel is one Garfunkel, the singing partner of Paul Simon

explanation.surface: The singer Sting supports the duo Simon & Garfunkel, perhaps for a large fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting looks like the singer, but it is the verb meaning to hurt sharply; 'Simon & Garfunkel' splits into an initial and a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that stings causes a sharp burning pain, and the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: European has the final word about pipe cleaner

indicators.note: about turns the closing word of a prayer round so it reads backwards

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A European has the last say on what tobacco-pipe cleaner to use.
explanation.walkthrough: A pipe cleaner suggests smokers' kit; here the pipe is the bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: This procedure flushes liquid into the rectum to clear the lower intestine, a tube of the body.

clue.text: Hesitate over rejecting a bachelor's joint

indicators.note: rejecting means one bachelor letter is thrown out
over means turned over, so the wavering word is read backwards

parts.note: to wobble is to waver or hesitate
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A bachelor hesitates over turning down someone's cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses WOBBLE to ELBBOW, and 'rejecting' drops one B.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinge in the middle of the arm is a body joint.

clue.text: Prize led school astray

definitions.note: prize as a verb: to value highly

indicators.note: astray means the letters of led and school wander out of their order

explanation.surface: A school was led off course in pursuit of an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like a noun for an award; it is the verb meaning to treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish something dearly is to keep it near you, embracing it, which is what valuing it means.

clue.text: Timeless card game is trying

indicators.note: read as time-less: the abbreviation for time is taken away from the card game

parts.note: Hearts is a trick-taking card game

explanation.surface: A card game that goes on endlessly is testing one's patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' splits into Time and less. 'trying' looks like tiresome; it is trying a case in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who presides over a case listens to it, so judicially examining is this verb.

clue.text: Ranch dressing leaves punters discontented

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, a drink made from leaves

indicators.note: discontented means the contents go, leaving only the outside letters of punters

parts.note: first and last letters of punters

explanation.surface: A salad dressing called ranch puts customers off their food.
explanation.walkthrough: Ranch dressing is a salad dressing; here it is what a cowboy wears on a ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboys wear leather leggings over their trousers when riding, so they are ranch clothing.

clue.text: 'Bucket', etc, translated right twice by one typing

indicators.text: translated right twice by one typing
indicators.note: on a QWERTY keyboard each letter of etc is moved two keys to the right, as a typist with misplaced hands would do

explanation.surface: Someone typing the word bucket and similar words keeps slipping on the keys.
explanation.walkthrough: On a QWERTY keyboard, two keys right of E is T, of T is U, and of C is B, so ETC becomes TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide open container for water, like a pail, can be called by either word.

clue.text: Old man takes drug when heading to adult parties extremely late

indicators.note: takes means the father word holds the drug letter inside it

parts.note: dad, one's old man, is a father
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: heading to asks for the first letter of adult

parts.note: first letter of adult
a do is a party, so two of them make parties

explanation.surface: A father takes drugs on his way to adult parties and stays out very late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means deceased, not tardy, so 'extremely late' is utterly dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird gives an idiom for something completely dead, and the late are the dead.

clue.text: Some depressing drinkers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: depressing things or experiences, also sedative drugs
second meaning: those who down drinks

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a remark about gloomy people in a pub; one word covers both depressing things and people who down drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedative pills and dispiriting events are both called this, and someone downing a pint is literally one too.

clue.text: Impressed by pieces, say, editor undertook

indicators.note: impressed by means the answer is pressed into the run of words that follows, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An editor who was impressed by some articles took on a commission.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'pieces', all of 'say' and the start of 'editor'.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, so the past tense means tried or took on.
